cross_references.notes: All primary sources (WHO, CDC, Africa CDC, ECDC, State Dept, MoH via CDC) agree on 2 countries with confirmed cases and 9+ health zones in Ituri; WHO May 20 DG briefing (51 confirmed DRC) supersedes CDC May 19 figure (34 confirmed DRC), reflecting rapid 24-hour escalation; death toll figures range 130-139 across sources dated May 19-20, with WHO May 20 being most current at ~139 suspected deaths.

locations.name: Mongbwalu Health Zone
locations.notes: Suspected index location; a high-traffic gold-mining town where WHO received first alert of unknown illness on 5 May 2026; outbreak thought to have originated here with mining-related population movement amplifying spread.

locations.name: Rwampara Health Zone
locations.notes: Six confirmed cases among 13 samples analysed by INRB; 6 health areas affected; initial Xpert tests returned false-negatives before INRB PCR confirmed Bundibugyo virus on 15 May.

locations.name: Bunia Health Zone
locations.notes: Capital of Ituri Province and major urban hub; site of first known suspected death (health worker, onset 24 April); hospitals became overwhelmed by 18 May, prompting establishment of field hospitals; American Dr. Peter Stafford confirmed infected here.

locations.name: Nyakunde
locations.notes: Confirmed cases reported in Nyakunde as of 20 May 2026, per NPR and PBS citing WHO; part of the expanding footprint across Ituri Province.

locations.name: Goma
locations.notes: Confirmed case: wife of a man who died of Ebola in Bunia travelled to Goma while infected; city of over 1 million under M23 rebel control on the Rwandan border; WHO DG May 20 briefing confirmed Goma as part of active case cluster.

locations.name: Butembo
locations.notes: Confirmed cases reported in Butembo as of 19-20 May, per UN News (WHO rep Dr. Ancia) and NPR; major urban centre with over 800,000 residents, previously epicentre of 2018-2020 Zaire ebolavirus outbreak.

locations.name: Kampala
locations.notes: Two confirmed imported cases (no apparent epidemiological link to each other), both in individuals who had travelled from DRC; first case: 59-year-old Congolese male admitted to Kibuli Muslim Hospital 11 May, died 14 May; second confirmed 16 May; no local transmission identified at time of reporting.

locations.name: Fort Portal
locations.notes: Group of Ugandans who attended a burial in eastern DRC returned to Uganda; some developed Ebola symptoms and were taken to Fort Portal for treatment, per Wikipedia citing AP; status under active investigation.

alerts.title: PHEIC Declared — Bundibugyo Ebola, DRC & Uganda
alerts.body: WHO Director-General declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 16 May 2026 — the first time in WHO history this was done before convening an Emergency Committee. As of 20 May, 51 confirmed DRC cases (Ituri and North Kivu) plus 2 confirmed in Uganda; ~600 suspected cases and ~139 suspected deaths. No approved vaccine or therapeutic exists for Bundibugyo virus.

alerts.title: PHECS Declared by Africa CDC (18 May 2026)
alerts.body: Africa CDC declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security on 18 May, empowering it to lead continental coordination. At the time of declaration ~395 suspected cases and 106 deaths; deep concern expressed over spread risk to Rwanda and South Sudan.

alerts.title: No Approved Vaccine or Therapeutic for Bundibugyo Virus
alerts.body: Both licensed Ebola vaccines (Ervebo by Merck, Zabdeno/Mvabea by J&J) target Zaire ebolavirus and have been explicitly confirmed as not effective against Bundibugyo. CDC and WHO confirm no approved prophylactics or therapeutics; experimental mAb and mRNA candidates are pre-clinical only and at least 2 months from potential availability.

alerts.title: Spread to North Kivu: Goma and Butembo Confirmed
alerts.body: Confirmed cases have reached Goma (a city of over 1 million under M23 rebel control on the Rwandan border) and Butembo in North Kivu Province, beyond the Ituri epicentre. WHO assesses regional risk as HIGH; neighbouring countries including Rwanda, South Sudan and Burundi are on high alert.

alerts.title: US Title 42 Entry Restrictions: DRC, Uganda, South Sudan
alerts.body: US CDC and DHS invoked Title 42 on 18 May 2026, barring entry of non-US nationals who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan within 21 days. The State Department issued Level 4 (Do Not Travel) advisories for all three countries and Level 3 (Reconsider Travel) for Rwanda.

alerts.title: American Healthcare Worker Infected; Evacuated to Germany
alerts.body: Dr. Peter Stafford, an American medical missionary (Serge organization) working in Ituri, tested positive on 17 May 2026 and was safely evacuated to Germany. Six high-risk American contacts were also evacuated to Germany for observation; none are being repatriated to the US.

alerts.title: Diagnostic Delay: Xpert Tests Returned False Negatives
alerts.body: Standard Ebola Xpert field tests target Zaire ebolavirus and returned false negatives on 20 Bundibugyo samples, causing a 3-4 week diagnostic delay that allowed hundreds of cases and multiple deaths before outbreak confirmation. BDBV is ~30% genetically divergent from Zaire ebolavirus.

alerts.title: US Commits $23M + Funding for Up to 50 Treatment Clinics
alerts.body: The US State Department mobilised an initial $23 million in bilateral assistance on 17-18 May and on 19 May announced funding for up to 50 Ebola response clinics in affected regions of DRC and Uganda, including support for surveillance, lab capacity, safe burials and clinical case management.

news.title: WHO chief alarmed by 'scale and speed' of Ebola as 600 suspected cases reported
news.summary: In a May 20 address to the World Health Assembly, WHO DG Tedros confirmed 51 cases laboratory-confirmed in DRC (Ituri and North Kivu including Goma) plus 2 in Uganda, with nearly 600 suspected cases and 139 suspected deaths. Tedros said the outbreak warrants 'serious concern' and the Emergency Committee agreed it is a PHEIC but not a pandemic emergency.

news.title: US State Dept issues Level 4 'Do Not Travel' for DRC, Uganda, South Sudan amid Ebola
news.summary: On 19 May 2026 the State Department issued Level 4 Do Not Travel advisories for DRC, Uganda and South Sudan, implementing CDC's Title 42 order restricting entry of any foreign nationals from those countries within 21 days. The US also committed to funding up to 50 Ebola response clinics alongside an initial $23 million bilateral aid package.

news.title: Ebola reaches Butembo and Goma; WHO rep says outbreak 'not two months from done'
news.summary: UN News reported that WHO's Dr. Ancia, speaking from Bunia, confirmed Ebola cases in Butembo and Goma (North Kivu) and warned the outbreak could last two years as with the 2018-2020 epidemic. UNHCR noted over 2 million displaced people in Ituri and North Kivu, with 11,000 South Sudanese refugees in Ituri needing preventive assistance.

news.title: American physician Dr. Peter Stafford safely evacuated from DRC to Germany for Ebola care
news.summary: CDC confirmed on 19 May that Dr. Peter Stafford — a medical missionary with Serge who contracted Bundibugyo virus while treating patients in Ituri — has been successfully evacuated to Germany, along with six high-risk American contacts. CDC stated Germany was chosen for its proximity and prior experience treating Ebola patients.

news.title: CDC and DHS invoke Title 42; entry ban for non-US nationals from DRC, Uganda, South Sudan
news.summary: On 18 May 2026, CDC and the Department of Homeland Security implemented Title 42 travel restrictions blocking entry of non-US passport holders who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan within 21 days. Enhanced screening was also deployed at US ports of entry for arrivals from affected regions.

news.title: Africa CDC declares Bundibugyo Ebola a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security
news.summary: On 18 May Africa CDC formally declared a PHECS under Article 3F of its statute, citing ~395 suspected cases, 106 deaths, and deep concern over cross-border spread risk to Rwanda and South Sudan. The declaration empowers Africa CDC to lead and coordinate a continental-level response.

news.title: Ebola outbreak raises questions about funding cuts and delayed detection — NPR
news.summary: NPR reported that the sheer number of cases before detection suggests the virus circulated for weeks undetected, with epidemiologists linking the delay to cuts in global health surveillance programs including USAID. The Bundibugyo strain's ~30% genetic divergence from Zaire ebolavirus caused field Xpert tests to return false negatives.

news.title: CDC confirms 9 health zones affected in Ituri; activates Emergency Response Center
news.summary: CDC's Ebola Response Incident Manager Dr. Satish Pillai confirmed in a May 17 briefing that the outbreak has now affected at least 9 health zones in Ituri Province and that CDC has activated its Emergency Response Center. CDC is deploying technical experts from Atlanta and working through its DRC country office to support surveillance and contact tracing.

news.title: WHO declares Ebola PHEIC — first DG declaration without Emergency Committee in WHO history
news.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros declared the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak a PHEIC on 16 May 2026, citing the high positivity rate in initial samples, spread to Kampala, and rising suspected cases and deaths. This marked the first time a WHO DG exercised Article 12 authority to declare a PHEIC without first convening an Emergency Committee.

news.title: No approved vaccine for Bundibugyo; mAb and mRNA candidates still pre-clinical
news.summary: NBC News and CDC confirmed there are no FDA-approved vaccines or therapeutics for Bundibugyo virus; the two licensed Ebola vaccines (Ervebo, Zabdeno/Mvabea) target Zaire ebolavirus and animal studies show they do not protect against Bundibugyo. CDC is exploring monoclonal antibody development and a Chinese mRNA candidate targeting three strains was published in PNAS on 19 May but remains pre-clinical.

news.title: Initial genomes from 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak confirm new spillover event
news.summary: Researchers at virological.org published initial genomic sequences from the May 2026 DRC/Uganda BDBV outbreak, confirming a new independent zoonotic spillover event distinct from the 2007 and 2012 lineages. The genomic data provide foundational information for medical countermeasure development.

news.title: ECDC: Outbreak likely larger than described; significant uncertainties remain
news.summary: ECDC's 19 May assessment confirmed over 500 suspected cases and 130 deaths in DRC, with one confirmed case in Goma (North Kivu), noting that 'significant uncertainties remain regarding the scale of transmission, and the outbreak is likely larger than currently described.' ECDC is sending experts to the region to assist response.

background.virus: Bundibugyo virus (BDBV); formal species name Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense
background.discovery: 2007, during an outbreak in Bundibugyo District, Uganda; genomic sequencing confirmed a novel species distinct from Zaire ebolavirus by ~30% genetic divergence
background.transmission: Direct contact with blood, body fluids, or tissues of infected people or animals; contact with contaminated surfaces, fomites, or bodies of deceased individuals. Individuals are infectious only when symptomatic. Fruit bats are the suspected zoonotic reservoir.
background.symptoms: Sudden fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, sore throat — followed by vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, rash, impaired kidney/liver function, internal and external bleeding; nosebleeds and vomiting blood reported in current outbreak. Most current DRC cases are aged 20–39 and two-thirds are female (CDC).
background.vaccines_therapeutics: No approved vaccine/therapeutic for BDBV; Ervebo & Zabdeno/Mvabea target Zaire only; mAb & mRNA candidates pre-clinical

past_outbreaks.notes: First identified outbreak; led to discovery and naming of the Bundibugyo strain; genomic sequencing confirmed a novel Orthoebolavirus species.
Second documented Bundibugyo outbreak; contained within months in a remote area; second and last BDBV outbreak prior to 2026.

Second-largest Ebola outbreak in history, different species (Zaire ebolavirus), but same geographic zone and containment challenges (insecurity, mobile populations, mistrust); directly relevant precedent for current response difficulties.

past_outbreaks.location: Ituri Province (epicentre: Mongbwalu, Rwampara, Bunia, Nyakunde) and North Kivu Province (Goma, Butembo) — DRC; Kampala and Fort Portal — Uganda
past_outbreaks.cfr: ~25–50% historical range for BDBV; current crude CFR undetermined due to large suspected-case denominator and diagnostic lag
past_outbreaks.notes: Third and largest Bundibugyo outbreak ever recorded; PHEIC declared by WHO 16 May 2026 (first-ever without Emergency Committee), PHECS declared by Africa CDC 18 May 2026; 9+ health zones in Ituri plus confirmed spread to Goma and Butembo (North Kivu); 2 confirmed imported cases in Kampala plus emerging cases near Fort Portal, Uganda; no approved vaccine or therapeutic; 3-week diagnostic delay from false-negative Xpert tests; virological.org genome sequences confirm new independent spillover event; American physician (Dr. Peter Stafford) confirmed infected 17 May, evacuated to Germany 19 May; US Title 42 restrictions invoked 18 May; $23M US bilateral aid pledged plus up to 50 treatment clinics.

why_this_matters: As of 20 May 2026, WHO confirmed 51 laboratory-confirmed cases in DRC (Ituri and North Kivu) plus 2 in Uganda, with ~600 suspected cases and ~139 suspected deaths — making this already the largest Bundibugyo outbreak ever recorded by a factor of more than 4× the previous largest, with case counts still accelerating (26 new confirmed and 143 new suspected in just 24–48 hours as of 19 May).

No approved vaccines or therapeutics exist for Bundibugyo virus; the two licensed Ebola vaccines (Ervebo, Zabdeno/Mvabea) target Zaire ebolavirus and are explicitly confirmed not effective against BDBV; experimental mAb and mRNA vaccine candidates remain pre-clinical, with WHO field staff warning a vaccine is at least two months away.

The outbreak has expanded beyond the Ituri epicentre to Goma and Butembo in North Kivu, representing a dangerous escalation: Goma is a city of over 1 million on the Rwandan border under M23 rebel control, presenting acute cross-border transmission risk; Butembo was the epicentre of the devastating 2018–2020 Zaire ebolavirus outbreak and has a traumatised, mistrustful population.

The outbreak zone lies within an active armed conflict; M23 rebels control Goma and impede access, contact tracing, and safe burial operations; healthcare workers have been killed and extreme population mobility — including mining-related movement from Mongbwalu — has amplified spread across multiple health zones.

Standard Ebola Xpert field tests returned false negatives because they target Zaire ebolavirus; BDBV's ~30% genetic divergence caused a 3–4 week diagnostic delay, allowing hundreds of cases to accumulate before confirmation — a critical surveillance gap directly enabled outbreak momentum, as noted by epidemiologists including Jennifer Nuzzo and Matthew Kavanagh.

Virological.org genomic sequences confirm this is a new independent zoonotic spillover event (not a re-emergence of 2007 or 2012 lineages), underlining that Bundibugyo virus poses recurring pandemic potential from an uncontrolled animal reservoir in a region with collapsing health systems.

International response is escalating: WHO Emergency Committee agreed PHEIC designation on 19 May; US deployed a DART team and committed $23M plus 50 treatment clinics; ECDC deployed experts; Germany received the first confirmed American patient; but cuts to global health funding — USAID programmes, CDC capacity, US withdrawal from WHO — have been widely cited by public health experts as contributing to the surveillance failure that allowed this outbreak to accelerate before detection.

WHO's representative in DRC warned that while a vaccine is at least two months away, 'it is not two months before the outbreak will be done — remember the previous one, it took two years,' underscoring that without a medical countermeasure, containment depends entirely on classic public-health tools (contact tracing, isolation, safe burials) in one of the world's most difficult operating environments.
